f: EST II Math Level 2 Strategic Approach
f_ar: EST II Math Level 2 Strategic Approach
b:
EST II Math Level 2 questions reward quick conceptual recognition. Key priorities include:

  • Algebraic Checks: Verify roots in original logarithmic and rational expressions to eliminate extraneous answers.
  • Geometric Visuals: Sketch vectors, complex plane points, and function graphs to verify signs and quadrants before calculating.

f: Definition 1.1 — The imaginary unit and complex numbers
f_ar: Definition 1.1 — The imaginary unit and complex numbers
b: The imaginary unit \( i \) is defined by \( i^2=-1 \). A complex number \( z=a+bi \) pairs a real part \( a \) with an imaginary part \( b \) (both real numbers). Two complex numbers are equal exactly when their real parts match and their imaginary parts match.
b_ar: The imaginary unit \( i \) is defined by \( i^2=-1 \). A complex number \( z=a+bi \) pairs a real part \( a \) with an imaginary part \( b \) (both real numbers). Two complex numbers are equal exactly when their real parts match and their imaginary parts match.

b:
Complex numbers add, subtract, and multiply using ordinary algebra, replacing \( i^2 \) with \( -1 \) wherever it appears. For \( z_1=a+bi \), \( z_2=c+di \):

\[ z_1\pm z_2=(a\pm c)+(b\pm d)i, \qquad z_1z_2=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i. \]

f: Theorem 1.1 — Complex roots of a quadratic
f_ar: Theorem 1.1 — Complex roots of a quadratic
b:
For \( ax^2+bx+c=0 \) with real \( a,b,c \) (\( a\neq0 \)) and discriminant \( \Delta=b^2-4ac<0 \), the two roots are the complex conjugate pair

\[ x=-\frac{b}{2a}\pm i\,\frac{\sqrt{4ac-b^2}}{2a}. \]
b_ar:
For \( ax^2+bx+c=0 \) with real \( a,b,c \) (\( a\neq0 \)) and discriminant \( \Delta=b^2-4ac<0 \), the two roots are the complex conjugate pair

\[ x=-\frac{b}{2a}\pm i\,\frac{\sqrt{4ac-b^2}}{2a}. \]

b: A conjugate pair \( a\pm bi \) always has equal modulus for both roots
b_ar: A conjugate pair \( a\pm bi \) always has equal modulus for both roots

b:
A sequence \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a constant \( d \): \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit formula is

\[ a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. \]
b_ar:
A sequence \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a constant \( d \): \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit formula is

\[ a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. \]

b:
The sum of an arithmetic sequence's first \( n \) terms is

\[ S_n=\frac{n}{2}\big(a_1+a_n\big)=\frac{n}{2}\big(2a_1+(n-1)d\big). \]
b_ar:
The sum of an arithmetic sequence's first \( n \) terms is

\[ S_n=\frac{n}{2}\big(a_1+a_n\big)=\frac{n}{2}\big(2a_1+(n-1)d\big). \]

b:
A sequence is geometric if consecutive terms share a constant ratio \( r\neq0 \): \( a_{n+1}=r\,a_n \), with explicit formula

\[ a_n=a_1\,r^{\,n-1}. \]
b_ar:
A sequence is geometric if consecutive terms share a constant ratio \( r\neq0 \): \( a_{n+1}=r\,a_n \), with explicit formula

\[ a_n=a_1\,r^{\,n-1}. \]

b:
For \( r\neq1 \), the sum of the first \( n \) terms of a geometric sequence is

\[ S_n=\frac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}. \]
b_ar:
For \( r\neq1 \), the sum of the first \( n \) terms of a geometric sequence is

\[ S_n=\frac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}. \]

b:
If \( |r|<1 \), the infinite geometric series converges to

\[ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}. \] If \( |r|\geq1 \) (and \( a_1\neq0 \)), the series diverges.

b: Starting from a base function \( f(x) \), the transformed function \( g(x)=a\,f(x-h)+k \) applies, in this order: a horizontal shift by \( h \) (right if \( h>0 \)), a vertical stretch/compression and reflection by \( a \) (a reflection over the \( x \)-axis if \( a<0 \)), and a vertical shift by \( k \).

b: A function is even if \( f(-x)=f(x) \) for every \( x \) in its domain (graph symmetric about the \( y \)-axis). A function is odd if \( f(-x)=-f(x) \) for every \( x \) (graph symmetric about the origin — a \( 180^\circ \) rotation of itself). Most functions are neither.

f: Theorem 3.1 — Even/odd powers determine even/odd polynomials
f_ar: Theorem 3.1 — Even/odd powers determine even/odd polynomials
b: A polynomial made up only of even-degree terms (including a constant) is an even function; a polynomial made up only of odd-degree terms is an odd function.
b_ar: A polynomial made up only of even-degree terms (including a constant) is an even function; a polynomial made up only of odd-degree terms is an odd function.

b: Two formula types automatically restrict a function's domain: a square root \( \sqrt{g(x)} \) requires \( g(x)\geq0 \), and a rational expression \( \dfrac{1}{g(x)} \) requires \( g(x)\neq0 \).
b_ar: Two formula types automatically restrict a function's domain: a square root \( \sqrt{g(x)} \) requires \( g(x)\geq0 \), and a rational expression \( \dfrac{1}{g(x)} \) requires \( g(x)\neq0 \).

b: A piecewise function is defined by different formulas on different parts of its domain. To evaluate it at a specific input, first identify which piece's condition that input satisfies, then apply only that piece's formula.

f: Definition 4.1 — Matrix, addition, and scalar multiplication
f_ar: Definition 4.1 — Matrix, addition, and scalar multiplication
b:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns. Two matrices of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]
b_ar:
An \( m\times n \) matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with \( m \) rows and \( n \) columns. Two matrices of the same dimensions add entrywise, and a scalar \( k \) multiplies every entry:

\[ (A+B)_{ij}=a_{ij}+b_{ij}, \qquad (kA)_{ij}=k\,a_{ij}. \]

b: If \( A \) is \( m\times n \) and \( B \) is \( n\times p \), the product \( AB \) is the \( m\times p \) matrix whose \( (i,j) \) entry is the dot product of row \( i \) of \( A \) with column \( j \) of \( B \): \[ (AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik}b_{kj}. \] Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.
b_ar: If \( A \) is \( m\times n \) and \( B \) is \( n\times p \), the product \( AB \) is the \( m\times p \) matrix whose \( (i,j) \) entry is the dot product of row \( i \) of \( A \) with column \( j \) of \( B \): \[ (AB)_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik}b_{kj}. \] Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.

f: Definition 4.3 — Determinant and the identity matrix
f_ar: تعريف 4.3 — المحدد and the المتطابقة المصفوفة
b: For \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is \( \det A=ad-bc \). The identity matrix \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \).
b_ar: For \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \), the determinant is \( \det A=ad-bc \). The identity matrix \( I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix} \) satisfies \( IA=AI=A \).

b:
If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \det A=ad-bc\neq0 \), then

\[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}. \] If \( \det A=0 \), no inverse exists.
b_ar:
If \( A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix} \) and \( \det A=ad-bc\neq0 \), then

\[ A^{-1}=\frac{1}{\det A}\begin{bmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{bmatrix}. \] If \( \det A=0 \), no inverse exists.

f: Definition 4.4 — Vectors: magnitude and dot product
f_ar: تعريف 4.4 — المتجهات: magnitude and dot product
b: A vector \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is \( \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2 \).
b_ar: A vector \( \mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle \) has magnitude \( |\mathbf{u}|=\sqrt{u_1^2+u_2^2} \). The dot product of \( \mathbf{u} \) and \( \mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2\rangle \) is \( \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2 \).

b: For nonzero vectors with angle \( \theta \) between them, \[ \cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}|\,|\mathbf{v}|}. \]
b_ar: For nonzero vectors with angle \( \theta \) between them, \[ \cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}|\,|\mathbf{v}|}. \]

b:
The derivative of \( f \) at \( x \), written \( f'(x) \), is defined as the limit of the difference quotient:

\[ f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}, \]

when that limit exists. It measures the instantaneous rate of change of \( f \) at \( x\) — the slope of the line tangent to \( f \)'s graph there.

b:
For a sample space \( S \) of equally likely outcomes and an event \( E\subseteq S \), the probability of \( E \) is

\[ P(E)=\frac{n(E)}{n(S)}, \]

where \( n(E) \) and \( n(S) \) count outcomes. Always \( 0\leq P(E)\leq1 \).
b_ar:
For a sample space \( S \) of equally likely outcomes and an event \( E\subseteq S \), the probability of \( E \) is

\[ P(E)=\frac{n(E)}{n(S)}, \]

where \( n(E) \) and \( n(S) \) count outcomes. Always \( 0\leq P(E)\leq1 \).

b: The complement of event \( E \), written \( E' \), is “\( E \) does not happen.” Since \( E \) and \( E' \) together account for every outcome exactly once, \[ P(E')=1-P(E). \]
